name: Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
summary: Overnight occupancy is restricted to the places and durations listed in Forest Order 19-24-05; this is a separate unit from Tahoe National Forest.
vehicleRule: A forest road or roadside parking space is not an authorized overnight location merely because driving or parking is permitted.
exceptions: Use only the exempt locations in Exhibits A and B and comply with their stay limits.
Order effective June 28, 2024 through December 1, 2027; check for replacements.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Eldorado National Forest
summary: Drive-to dispersed camping is described as available on most forest land unless specifically prohibited. Undeveloped camping is limited to 10 days per ranger district per calendar year.
vehicleRule: Keep vehicles on designated roads/trails; park within one vehicle length of the road or trail surface edge. Confirm the route is open to your vehicle on the current MVUM.
exceptions: Choose a spot at least 100 feet from lakes and streams.
Stay outside developed-campground boundaries; current orders and seasonal road closures still apply.
The annual-limit order has separate exceptions for specified wilderness areas and the Pacific Crest Trail.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Inyo National Forest
summary: Dispersed camping is available outside mapped Restricted Recreation Areas. Stay limits are 14 consecutive days at one location and 28 days per calendar year forest-wide; relocation must be at least 10 miles.
vehicleRule: Stay on established roads and do not drive off-road to camp. Use a cleared durable surface and verify that the precise pullout lies outside the Restricted Recreation Area boundary.
exceptions: At least 200 feet from water.
Within Restricted Recreation Areas, camping is limited to developed campground campsites or posted overflow areas.
Order 05-04-50-25-17 runs through July 3, 2027; local closures may add restrictions.

sources.label: Camping guidance and interactive restricted-area map

scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Tahoe National Forest
summary: Roadside camping has significant mapped exclusions. Truckee/Sierraville Restricted Use Areas prohibit camping, including on roads and trails, except for specifically allowed places.
vehicleRule: An open MVUM road does not override a camping-restriction area. Check the exact location against Order 17-25-05 and the Highway 20 order before treating a roadside stop as an overnight option.
exceptions: East-side restricted areas: approved campgrounds/designated dispersed sites and specified trail corridors only; a hiking-corridor exemption does not authorize driving there.
Highway 20: mapped half-mile and quarter-mile buffers and Conservation Camp Road restrictions under Order 17-25-01.
The Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit has its own more restrictive overnight order.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Mendocino National Forest
summary: Dispersed camping is described as available outside developed sites, but camping within one mile of a developed recreation site is prohibited.
vehicleRule: Use roads open to your vehicle on the current MVUM and an existing impacted site. The inspected guidance gives no universal off-road pullout distance; do not infer one.
exceptions: Remain at least 150 feet from water.
Developed recreation sites include campgrounds, picnic areas and trailheads; the one-mile exclusion matters even when an adjacent road is open.
Within the same one-mile-radius location: at most 14 days in any 30-day period and 28 cumulative days in any 12-month period.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Shasta-Trinity National Forest
summary: Dispersed camping is broadly described as available, but the published roadside parking and campsite setback instructions do not clearly authorize sleeping inside a roadside vehicle.
vehicleRule: The leaflet limits parking to one vehicle length from a designated road, while both the leaflet and current camping page say camps must be at least 200 feet from roads. Ask the ranger district how this applies to sleeping in the car at the proposed pullout.
exceptions: No dispersed camping at Lewiston Lake or in the Mt. Shasta plantations area.
Other exclusions include restricted nesting areas and mapped no-camping zones.
Published guidance also separates camps from developed sites, trailheads, private property and state highways.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Sierra National Forest
summary: The forest describes choosing your own dispersed spot as an option throughout most of the forest. That broad description does not identify every legal car-sleeping pullout.
vehicleRule: Use the current MVUM to verify the route, vehicle class and dates. The inspected forest pages do not establish a universal vehicle pull-off distance or blanket roadside sleeping permission.
exceptions: Opening and closing dates can change without notice for weather or safety.
Check current forest orders, exact land ownership and the site before overnighting; this entry is general policy evidence.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Plumas National Forest
summary: Official orders address dispersed campsites and limit their occupancy, but they do not identify all permitted roadside car-sleeping locations.
vehicleRule: Check the current MVUM for vehicle access and seasonal allowances. No forest-wide roadside pull-off distance was verified in the inspected sources.
exceptions: Dispersed camping is limited to 14 days per ranger district per calendar year; total forest camping is limited to 30 days per calendar year.
Individual campsites are limited to eight people and two vehicles.
Check local no-camping/closure orders and exact site conditions; limits alone are not a grant of permission.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Stanislaus National Forest
summary: Dispersed roadside camping can be reached by graded dirt roads where local restrictions permit; use an existing site. The forest limits dispersed camping to 21 total days per ranger district per calendar year.
vehicleRule: Use the MVUM for the road system and confirm the road is suitable for the car. No universal off-road pullout distance is stated in the inspected forest guidance.
exceptions: Keep camps at least 150 feet from streams or other water.
Dispersed camping is typically not allowed near developed campgrounds, picnic areas or trailheads.
Current closures, Cherry Lake restrictions, fire rules and seasonal access must be checked.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Gifford Pinchot National Forest
summary: Motorized access to dispersed camps exists along specified MVUM corridors, not every open road. The current map and its tables identify the eligible locations.
vehicleRule: Where designated, use only existing routes within 150 feet of the main road; highway-legal vehicles only, without resource damage. Do not create a route or drive farther than 150 feet.
exceptions: Some roads do not permit motorized access to dispersed camps; absent corridor symbols do not grant access.
Stay at least 100 feet from water and out of fragile meadows/restricted areas.
After 14 consecutive camping days, leave the forest; current closures still apply.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Mt. Hood National Forest
summary: Dispersed camping is described as an option outside developed sites, with specific closed roads and sensitive areas excluded. The general camping page does not independently establish car-sleeping permission at an arbitrary pullout.
vehicleRule: Use the MVUM for vehicle access and an existing impacted site. No blanket off-road driving distance was verified in the inspected forest guidance.
exceptions: Camping is closed in developed recreation sites, along some roads and in sensitive areas; ask the district for details.
Camp at least 100 feet from streams, rivers and lakes.
Maximum 14 consecutive days in one location and 28 days forest-wide per calendar year.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Deschutes National Forest
summary: Motorized dispersed camping access is route-specific. The current MVUM publishes vehicle classes, seasons and off-route distance allowances.
vehicleRule: The 2011 travel decision allows access within 300 feet only on routes shown open to that use, to existing/designated/defined sites, no closer than 30 feet to water. Confirm the current MVUM for the exact route; the historical decision is not a current closure check.
exceptions: Routes absent from the current MVUM are not open to public motor vehicles.
Current area closures, including active alerts around Bend, can override the underlying travel designation.
Do not create tracks or treat an open driving road as automatic camping permission.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Coconino National Forest
summary: Motorized dispersed camping is limited to road segments specifically designated for dispersed camping. Camping and campfire restriction areas are shown separately.
vehicleRule: The 2025 travel map permits dispersed-camping vehicle use only within 300 feet of the edge of designated camping road segments on National Forest System land. Road-edge parking with a walk to a camp is a separate allowance.
exceptions: The travel map identifies prohibited camping locations in Flagstaff and Sedona city limits.
Check current MVUM, forest orders and local designated-site-only restrictions before using a pullout.
Keep the traveled roadway clear; an open road without camping designation is not evidence of vehicle-camping access.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest
summary: Motorized dispersed-camping access depends on the ranger district and the exact MVUM camping table. There is no single forest-wide distance inferred here.
vehicleRule: For example, the 2025 Pleasant Grove MVUM lists specific roads allowing access 150 feet off the road centerline, with the same vehicle classes and dates as the road. Apply that allowance only where the relevant table and map designate it.
exceptions: The map distinguishes left-side, right-side and both-side camping corridors.
Other districts have their own maps and tables; never extend the Pleasant Grove allowance to another district.
Current camping restrictions, water setbacks and emergency closures remain separate checks.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: White River National Forest
summary: The forest describes dispersed camping along roads shown on its MVUM. Some areas allow only designated sites or use shorter stay limits.
vehicleRule: Choose an already impacted site no more than 300 feet from the road centerline and at least 100 feet from water; confirm the exact road and season on the current MVUM.
exceptions: Some locations restrict dispersed camping to designated sites or seven-day stays.
Unless otherwise noted, maximum 14 days within 30 days, then relocate outside a 20-mile radius.
Site-specific regulations, current orders and seasonal access override general guidance.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks
